question.problem: Given the inequalities $-1<x<4$ and $x>2$, express their common set of solutions as an interval.
question.worked_solution:
We start by sketching the solutions to the two inequalities separately:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14248994/assets/f9409f298a0f4d1fd06bdac159e8fd7eb034ee577d2c8956730f0cc3919e051a.png)

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14248994/assets/f4fd2c61f600408511d967690cf02c95a3d2fa470aa5d7e9176a222d16823d5b.png)

The common set of values consists of the values that are in both intervals. So, it can be graphed by finding where the two intervals overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14248994/assets/fdf3410c69cf8559abfb7b223fc175bd1704d6334c8abbceb45240c894514172.png)

Therefore, the common set of values is
$(2,4).$
